description_en: Approximately 2.5 kilometers north of the Gokarṇeśvara temple (GKN0010) lies a locality called Bālūvā gāũ (Suntākhānā). Situated along the bank of therājkulo(royal canal), the site features an aniconic stone worshipped as Mahākāla and a stonecaityadating to the Licchavi period. The remains of scatteredcaityashave been restored through recent conservation work. Adjacent to thecaitya, a two-storied temple has been erected above the ancient Mahākāla stone, enshrining a newly installed anthropomorphic image of the deity.The historical significance of this location became evident following the discovery of an Aṃśuvarmā-period inscription in 1989 CE  (VS 2046), which was later studied by Ś. Rājavaṃśī (VS 2052, p. ñ). The inscription, now securely reinstalled on the site, is dated to 614 CE (Saṃvat 536) and attests to the existence of a substantial Licchavi-era monastery namedRājavihāra. The prefix “rāja-” in its title, according to the inscription, signifies that the monastery was commissioned by King Aṃśuvarmā himself (Ś. Rājavaṃśī VS 2047, p. 22). Based on its proximity to the royal palace, Ś. Rājavaṃśī (VS 2056, pp. 160–162) further suggests that thisvihāramay have been located near theKailāsakuṭa Bhavana, the principal palace of Aṃśuvarmā’s reign.The inscription also reveals that this was a large royal monastery accommodating monks from all four directions, reflecting the cosmopolitan character of Buddhist monasticism during the Licchavi period. TheGopālarājavaṃśāvalī(folio 22) likewise records that Aṃśuvarmā established a monastery calledRājavihāra. The Hāḍigāũ inscription of Aṃśuvarmā’s year 32 further states that threepurāṇaand twopaṇawere to be allocated annually to thisvihāra, offering insight into its institutional and economic stature (D. Vajrācārya VS 2030, p. 320). Another Licchavi inscription from Patan, dated to Saṃvat 603, also mentionsRājavihāraand indicates that the monastery was accompanied by a drainage or water channel (kuloorḍhala), providing evidence of its architectural infrastructure (D. Vajrācārya VS 2036, p. 498).Over time, this once-grandvihāragradually declined, leaving behind only fragments ofcaityas. Until a few decades ago, however, the ancientrājkulāthat once flowed beside the site still remained functional (local resident, Thāpā, male, age 83). The rediscovery of the buried inscription in 1989 CE (VS 2046) brought to light these long-forgotten historical details.According to local belief, the original Mahākāla image that once stood here was transferred to the Tundikhel grounds by King Pratāpa Malla. In continuation of this local tradition, a new anthropomorphic image of Mahākāla was consecrated at the site in 2016 CE, replacing the earlier aniconic stone, and a two-storied temple was constructed above it. Apart from daily worship performed by the local residents, no regularguṭhīor elaborate ritual activities are currently maintained at the site.
description_ne: यहाँ प्राप्त अभिलेखबाट यो स्थानमा राजा अंशुवर्माले बनाएको ‘राजविहार’ नामक बौद्ध संरचना हुने गरेको तथ्य खुल्दछ ।गोकर्णेश्वर मन्दिरबाट (GKN0010) करिब २.५ किमी उत्तरमा बालुवागाउँ (सुन्ताखाना) कहलिएको ठाउँ छ । उक्त स्थानमा राजकुलोको डिलमा महाकालका रूपमा पुजिँदै आएको अमूर्त ढुङ्गा र लिच्छविकालीन शिलाचैत्य छ । यस स्थानमा छरपस्ट रूपमा रहेका चैत्यका अवशेषलाई जीर्णोद्धार गरी पुनर्स्थापना गरिएको छ । चैत्य समीपैमा महाकालको अमूर्त ढुङ्गा हुने गरेको स्थानमा पनि दुईतले मन्दिर उठाई महाकालको मूर्त प्रतिमा थपिएको छ ।बौद्ध अवशेष प्राप्त यस स्थानको ऐतिहासिकता निर्क्यौल हुनेगरी यहाँ विसं २०४६ सालमा अंशुवर्माकालीन अभिलेख फेला परेको थियो (Ś. Rājavaṃśī VS 2052, p. ञ) । उक्त अभिलेख हाल यसै स्थानमा सुरक्षित तवरले ठड्याइएको छ । संवत् ५३६ (सन् ६१४) को सो अभिलेखानुसार यहाँ राजविहार नामक ठुलै लिच्छविकालीन विहार भएको कुरा खुल्दछ । विहारको अगाडि ‘राज’ शब्द परेको यो विहार अंशुवर्माले नै बनाएको कुरा पनि प्राप्त अभिलेखबाट खुल्दछ (Ś. Rājavaṃśī VS 2047, p. 22) । Ś. Rājavaṃsī (VS 2056, pp. 160-162 ) ले दरबारको अवस्थिति नजिकै बनाइएको विहार भएकाबाट यो ‘राजविहार’ कहलिएको र उक्त दरबार कैलाशकूट हुन सक्ने अनुमान गरेका छन् । जे होस्, यहाँ लिच्छविकालमा राजाबाटै निर्मित ठुलो विहार भएको जसमा चारै दिशाबाट आएका भिक्षुहरू बस्दथे भन्ने तथ्य अभिलेखले खुलाएको छ । गोपालराजवंशावलीको पत्र २२ मा पनि अंशुवर्माले ‘राजविहार’ बनाएको प्रसंग छ (Gopālarājavaṃśāvalī fol. 22) । यस विहारका निम्ति अंशुवर्माकै संवत् ३२ को हाडिगाउँ अभिलेखमा प्रतिवर्ष ३ पुराण २ पण  दिनुपर्ने कुरा परेबाट यसको तात्कालिक स्तर प्रष्टिन्छ (D. Vajrācārya VS 2030, p. 320) । यसैगरी पाटनको संवत् ६०३ को अर्को लिच्छवि अभिलेखमा पनि राजविहारको उल्लेखन आउँछ जसबाट यस विहारसँगै कुलो वा ढल भएको तथ्य खुल्दछ (D. Vajrāchārya VS 2036, p. 498) ।कुनै समय ठुलो विहार भएको यो स्थान कालान्तरमा केही चैत्यका अवशेष बाहेक केही पनि नबचेको स्थितिमा पुग्यो । तर केहीवर्ष पूर्वसम्म यस स्थान हुँदै बग्ने ऐतिहासिक राजकुलो भने जीवन्त अवस्थामै थियो (local resident, Thāpā, male, age 83) ।  भाग्यवस् विसं २०४६ मा अभिलेख गाडिएको अवस्थामा भेटिए पश्चात् उल्लेखित तथ्य खुलेका हुन् ।बालुवागाउँका स्थानीय यहाँ प्राचीनकालदेखि पुँजिदै आएका महाकाल मूर्तिलाई प्रताप मल्लले टुँडिखेलमा स्थानान्तरण गरेको लोकविश्वास राख्छन् । उक्त लोकविश्वासको आधारमा यहाँ महाकाल भनिने अमूर्त ढुङ्गाको साटो सन् २०१६ मा मूर्त प्रतिमा स्थापना गरी दुईतले मन्दिर नै खडा गिरएको छ । दैनिक स्थानीयको सामान्य पूजा बाहेक यस स्थानमा अन्य केही विशेष पूजा एवं गुठीको व्यवस्था छैन ।

historical_events.event_description: This 614 CE Licchavi inscription is not directly related to the caitya, but it records that King Aṃśuvarmā remitted themalla kara(a form of state tax) that had been levied upon the inhabitants of Ahiduṃkoṭṭa-grāma—present-day Bālūvagā̃—where theRājavihārawas located.

The local residents of Bālūvagāṃ hold a long-standing belief that the ancient image of Mahākāla once enshrined at this site was transferred to Tundikhel by King Pratāpa Malla. On the basis of this local tradition, the aniconic stone formerly worshipped as Mahākāla was replaced in 2016 CE by a new anthropomorphic image, and a two-storied temple was constructed over it.
